introduction: The original Constitution of India (1950) contained Fundamental Rights but did NOT contain Fundamental Duties. These duties were added later to remind citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain moral and civic obligations towards the country, society, and fellow citizens.

core_concepts.title: Addition to the Constitution
core_concepts.description: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 during the National Emergency, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

core_concepts.title: Part and Article
core_concepts.description: They are placed in a newly created Part IVA of the Constitution, which consists of only one Article: Article 51A.

core_concepts.title: Source of Borrowing
core_concepts.description: The concept of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union). Notably, no major democratic country (like USA, Canada, France) has a list of duties for citizens except Japan.

core_concepts.title: Number of Duties
core_concepts.description: Originally, 10 duties were added in 1976. Later, one more duty was added, bringing the total to 11 current Fundamental Duties.

core_concepts.title: Non-Justiciable Nature
core_concepts.description: Like the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable. You cannot be taken to court directly for simply failing to perform them (unless backed by a specific law).

important_entities.name: Sardar Swaran Singh Committee
important_entities.significance: The Congress government appointed this committee in 1976 to make recommendations about fundamental duties, the need for which was felt during the internal emergency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Were they in the original Constitution?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common trap in exams. The answer is NO. The original constitution only had Rights and Directive Principles. Duties were added 26 years later in 1976.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Added by the 42nd Amendment Act. Placed in Part IV-A (4A).

exam_strategy_tips: The source country (USSR/Russia), the committee name (Swaran Singh), and the Amendment (42nd CAA, 1976) are the three most frequently asked questions at the beginner level.
